newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma amends PSA laws-agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma amends PSA laws-agency.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament passed amendments to production-sharing legislation in a first reading, Interfax news agency reported on Friday.

The results of the vote showed 290 deputies voted to pass the amendments bill, 23 against and one abstained. The bill must pass through two more readings in the Duma before it moves on to the upper house of parliament, the Federation Council.
It is unclear whether the Duma will have time to pass the bill through another reading before it breaks for the summer recess on June 24.
The proposed changes to the legislation determine the criteria according to which reserves eligible for development under production-sharing agreements are selected, Interfax said.
Two lists will be set up - one for existing reserves and another for future deposits.
Talks may be held and deals made between the government and the investor involved on reserves appearing in the first of the two lists.
But prospective deposits will only be eligible for technical-economic assessment and government analysis, Alexei Mikhailov, head of the Duma's natural resources committee, was quoted as saying.

Mikhailov said that the amendments to the production-sharing law were aimed above all at protecting the interests of Russian producers, giving them preferential rights on carrying out work as subcontractors, transporters or in any other capacity.

The success of the bill in its first reading will be welcomed by western and Russian oil companies, who say production-sharing agreements are vital to Russia's oil and gas industries in the long term.

Delays in passing the list of reserves eligible for development under production-sharing agreements and changes to legislation to make them compatible with existing legislation are said to be holding up investments worth around $60 billion.
